title: DNS SVCB RFC 9461 Endpoint Selection Architecture
purpose: Define the RFC 9461 DNS SVCB endpoint-selection boundary for ALPN, port, dohpath, HTTPS SvcParam carry-through, and DoH path expansion.
design_summary: The selection slice stays in `Incursa.Quic.Dns` as pure scalar helpers. `DnsServiceBindingRecord` holds normalized SVCB data for authentication name, ALPN protocols, optional `dohpath`, optional `port`, and HTTPS SvcParams. `DnsServiceBindingSelectionOptions` records client ALPN support and whether the client respects the port key. `DnsServiceBindingSelector` returns compatible DNS endpoints only when ALPN or an equivalent supported key is present, ignores records with unsupported port keys, requires `dohpath` for HTTP ALPNs, uses per-protocol defaults when port is omitted, carries HTTPS SvcParams only to HTTP endpoints, and leaves actual DNS resolution/network I/O outside this layer.
data_and_state_considerations: The helpers do not query DNS, parse DNS wire RRs, create QUIC connections, or send DoH requests. They transform already-materialized SVCB scalar data into endpoint candidates and can be consumed later by resolver integration or ProtocolLab scenario adapters.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Records with no `alpn` and no recognized equivalent protocol key are incompatible.
DoH endpoint candidates require a relative `dohpath` URI template containing a `dns` variable.
If a client does not respect the SVCB `port` key, records carrying `port` are ignored.
When no `port` is present, DoT and DoQ default to 853 while DoH defaults to 443, producing separate endpoint candidates.
risks: This slice accepts materialized scalar SVCB data; DNS packet parsing and RRset ordering remain future work.
This slice validates and expands DoH path templates but does not send HTTP requests.
This slice does not implement SVCB AliasMode acceleration guidance or resolver fallback policy.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: Endpoint selection is kept separate from `DoqClient` and the core QUIC transport so future resolver integration can compose SVCB data with connection setup without moving DNS policy into packet, stream, or scheduler internals.
